particle_condition: Al 6061 powder, Solvus Global; gas-atomized; heat treatments in rotary tube furnace (atmosphere not stated); as-received (AR), as-atomized, no heat treatment
oxide_state: native Al-Mg oxide shell, TEM/EDS FWHM thickness 16.8 +/- 1.7 nm; as-received oxide described in prior work as more likely amorphous (Sec. 5)
vcr_definition: equal-count window (mid = v_cr): smallest impact group with equal numbers of rebound and bonding events, v_cr = mean of its highest and lowest velocity (Sec. 4); window bounds not printed
notes: AR. Dynamic yield strength Yd = 246.3 +/- 7.5 MPa (Table 1, from CoR fit, alpha = 0.7). AR is the strongest powder (fine as-solidified cells, heterogeneous phases). Authors' explanation (Sec. 4-5): heat treatment lowers strength (static by up to 38 %, dynamic by up to 34 %) and thickens the oxide (up to 47 %), and the two effects offset each other, so v_cr varies by at most 7.6 % from AR. Strength alone (Eq. 4, v_cr ~ (2/k)(C0/B) Yd; Fig. 7a) and oxide thickness alone (Fig. 7b) do not explain the trend. Combined model Eq. 6 (Lienhard rule of mixtures, sigma0 = 870 MPa, jet t = 100 nm, k = 0.062 fitted on AR, C0 = 5300 m/s, B = 67.55 GPa) fits best (Fig. 8); the authors judge the two effects about equal on average, with heat treatment acting more through the oxide (Fig. 9). No error bars in Fig. 6(b); window bounds not digitized from Fig. 5(a) (overlapping points at CoR = 0, not resolvable), so S1 window width is unavailable. Temperatures not stated (room assumed); impacts tested ~100-1000 m/s; velocity uncertainty +/-2 %.
